ask: Draft the move from hard STE rules to outcomes: for each of the five blocking codes, what outcome it was for, whether a CI check, a judge or nothing should carry it, and what ste_gate becomes. Include the word and line change.
note: Five STE codes still block edits: STE001 (sentence over 30 words), STE011 (bloat), STE013 (double negative), STE020 (button or label over 4 words) and STE021 (UI escape comment). Checked at 11f5e4f: settings.json runs ste_gate before every Markdown or UI write and blocks every such write if the script is missing; md_sweep runs at each turn end; CI's STE lint step already fails a PR on changed lines. Direction you agreed Oct 20: stop blocking at edit time; keep the cheap checks in CI on changed files only; drop STE020 for the icon and label rule (topic 'Spacing, motion and icons') and design review; the reply-style judges (c7) carry the outcome. Same principle as c21: checks run in CI or at commit, never per edit. Draft (batch 9), Oct 22: the gate and md_sweep turn every refusal into a note and still run per edit; STE001, STE011, STE013 and STE020 move to CI; STE021 optional; 719 STE001 refusals in 15 sessions from Oct 13 to 22, no incident named for any code. Advice sent Oct 22, not yet confirmed by you: approve with three changes. (1) Take both hooks out of settings.json instead of making them note-only, since a note that changes nothing is noise and the per-edit cost stays. This also settles the fail-closed question. If a hook stays, it fails open: it is a style check, not a safety guard, and a missing script must not block every Markdown write in every repo (advice Oct 22; safety guards like guard.py stay fail-closed). (2) Drop STE020 as agreed Oct 20, not move it to CI. (3) Fold STE021 away (0 fires). CI carries STE001, STE011 and STE013. Goal session report, Oct 22: STE hook removal built and reviewed, waiting for the next batch (batch 9). The ste-ci-carries lane is empty (its rule-list row moved with the removal). Open: CI's plain-English check reads Markdown only, so UI files lose the long-sentence, bloat and double-negative checks; the session took that as the default and asks whether UI files should be checked too. After it merges, rerun the installer (two stub scripts keep writes working until then). Landed, checked at claude-settings f463787 (main, Oct 25): the STE hooks left settings.json in #566 (batch-oct23a, Oct 23), after #564 dropped and the goal-2 session re-applied the lane. Left over: two exit-0 stubs, lint/ste_gate.py and lint/md_sweep.py, kept for old installs (debt ste-stubs-delete). Deleting them was a goal-2 lane; not done (unknown whether the session parked it on the install-log check).
title: Swap the hard STE rules for the outcomes they were meant to get
why: Your direction, Oct 20: STE went in as hard rules, but what you want is the outcome: plain replies you can follow, clear UI copy, short docs. The rules block edits, slow every edit, and fight plain-beats-short (c7).
